summary: LLM inference costs can be cut by 40-80% with a layered strategy combining prompt caching, semantic caching, model routing, and batch processing, without sacrificing quality. Prompt caching alone reduces API costs 45-80% and improves time-to-first-token 13-31%, while adding semantic caching and budget-aware routing has achieved 47% spend reduction in production. The biggest wins come from stacking exact-match, semantic, and prefix caches and instrumenting hit rate per layer.

techniques.name: Prompt (Prefix) Caching
techniques.description: Reuses the cached KV state for a matching prompt prefix (e.g. a long system prompt), so repeated input tokens are billed at a steep discount while the model still generates a fresh answer. Cache reads are billed as low as 0.05x input on Claude Sonnet, and OpenAI charges ~95% less for cached input tokens.
techniques.example: Place your stable 10,000-token system prompt and tool definitions first and mark a cache breakpoint so every subsequent agent turn reads the prefix at 0.05x cost instead of full input price.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Returns a stored answer for a semantically similar (not identical) request and skips the model call entirely, saving both input AND output tokens. Tools like vCache return cached responses under user-defined error-rate guarantees.
techniques.savings: ~18.9% additional savings on top of prompt caching; near-100% on cache hits
techniques.example: Embed incoming queries and, if cosine similarity to a cached query exceeds a threshold (e.g. 0.95), serve the stored response instead of calling the LLM — ideal for FAQ-style chatbots with high query repetition.

techniques.name: Exact-Match Caching
techniques.description: Caches responses keyed on an exact query hash, serving identical repeated queries at sub-millisecond latency with zero LLM inference. Forms the fastest first layer of a multi-tier cache.
techniques.savings: 100% on cache hits (eliminates the inference call)
techniques.example: Hash each deterministic request (temperature=0) and store the response in Redis; a repeated identical query returns instantly without touching the model.

techniques.name: Smart Model Routing & Cascading
techniques.description: Classifies task complexity and routes easy requests to cheap/budget-tier models while reserving expensive flagship models for hard tasks, with quality fallback logic. Semantic caching plus budget-aware routing hits 47% spend reduction in production.
techniques.example: Run a lightweight complexity classifier that sends simple classification/extraction to a small model like GPT-6.1 mini and only escalates ambiguous or multi-step reasoning tasks to a flagship model.

techniques.name: Batch APIs
techniques.description: Submits non-urgent requests through asynchronous batch endpoints for a flat 50% discount, and the discount stacks with caching. Ideal for workloads that can tolerate minutes-to-hours latency.
techniques.example: Send overnight document summarization or embedding-generation jobs via the Batch API instead of the real-time endpoint to automatically halve their cost.

techniques.name: Cap Output and Reasoning Tokens
techniques.description: Output tokens cost ~5x input on current Claude models, so limiting max_tokens and constraining reasoning effort directly cuts the most expensive part of a request.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens to a tight realistic limit and request concise answers, turning down reasoning effort for tasks that don't need deep chain-of-thought.

techniques.name: Structured Outputs & JSON Schemas
techniques.description: Enforcing a schema produces compact, parseable output and avoids verbose prose and retry loops caused by malformed responses, reducing wasted output tokens.
techniques.savings: 10-30% reduction in output tokens and retries
techniques.example: Use the provider's structured-output/JSON-schema mode to get exactly the fields you need, eliminating extra explanatory text and parse-failure retries.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression (LLMLingua)
techniques.description: Compresses long prompts and RAG contexts with minimal performance loss by dropping low-information tokens, particularly effective for long-context retrieval systems.
techniques.savings: Up to 50-80% prompt-token reduction in long contexts
techniques.example: Run retrieved RAG documents through LLMLingua before injection to shrink a 10,000-token context to a few thousand tokens while preserving answer quality.

techniques.name: Lean Prompt Engineering & Context Management
techniques.description: Keeping system prompts and rules files tight, compacting conversation history at phase boundaries, and limiting retrieval to a fixed token budget prioritizing relevance all cut recurring input cost on every call.
techniques.example: Cap your CLAUDE.md/rules file under 5,000 tokens and run /compact at natural task boundaries to compress conversation state instead of carrying full history.

techniques.name: Session Context Management
techniques.description: Maintains conversation state efficiently by summarizing or trimming prior turns rather than resending the full transcript on each request, avoiding redundant token growth in long chats.
techniques.example: Replace older conversation turns with a rolling summary so a 30-message chat sends a compact state object instead of thousands of accumulated tokens.

techniques.name: Open-Weight Model Offloading
techniques.description: Routes high-volume or privacy-sensitive workloads to self-hosted open-weight models (e.g. Llama, Qwen, Mistral) to eliminate per-token API fees entirely for suitable tasks.
techniques.savings: Up to 90%+ on offloaded high-volume workloads
techniques.example: Serve bulk classification or embedding generation on a self-hosted Llama model via vLLM, keeping only hard reasoning tasks on a paid frontier API.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic cache for LLM responses that stores and retrieves answers by embedding similarity, cutting repeated API calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); you pay only for your own vector store/embedding compute

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers offering model routing, fallbacks, caching, cost tracking, and budget limits through a single OpenAI-compatible API.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise/Cloud from ~$250/mo for teams

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and cost monitoring proxy with caching, request logging, prompt hit-rate analytics, and spend tracking per layer.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier up to 10k requests/mo; paid plans from ~$20/mo

tools.name: Redis Semantic Cache (LangCache)
tools.description: Redis-backed exact-match and semantic caching for LLM apps with sub-millisecond lookups, used to build multi-tier caching strategies.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis OSS free; Redis Cloud usage-based from ~$0 free tier upward

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in LLM caching (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic), model routing, and context management utilities.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression library that reduces prompt and RAG context tokens with minimal quality loss.

tools.name: vCache
tools.description: Semantic cache that returns responses for near-matching prompts under user-defined error-rate guarantees, saving both input and output tokens.

tools.name: Requesty
tools.description: LLM routing and caching gateway that layers prefix and semantic caching with budget-aware model routing and spend analytics.
tools.pricing_paid: Usage-based; free tier with paid pro plans

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway providing semantic/simple caching, load balancing, routing, and observability across many providers through one endpoint.

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference server for self-hosting open-weight models with KV-cache optimization and prefix caching.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); you pay only GPU infrastructure

quick_wins: Enable prompt/prefix caching by putting stable system prompts and tool definitions first with a cache breakpoint — 45-80% cost cut with near-zero code change.
Move all non-urgent jobs (summaries, embeddings, evals) to the Batch API for an immediate stacking 50% discount.
Cap max_tokens and reduce reasoning effort since output tokens cost ~5x input, trimming your most expensive token category.
Add an exact-match + semantic cache layer (Redis/GPTCache) to serve repeated and similar queries without any LLM call.
Route easy tasks to a cheap budget-tier model via LiteLLM or a gateway, reserving flagship models only for hard reasoning tasks.
